subject: Migration evaluation: next steps & compatibility checklist
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Rao <priya.rao@mayatech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-12T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Migration evaluation: next steps & compatibility checklist

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed plan so we’re aligned before we spin up the PoC sandbox. Great call — your team’s priorities (model parity, predictable cost, and minimum engineering churn) are clear and map well to what we can test quickly.

Call highlights:
- Primary goal: validate that MayaTech can migrate inference from its current hyperscaler endpoints to a Redwood-hosted/Dedicated deployment with minimal changes to clients.
- Key evaluation axes: API/SDK compatibility (OpenAI-compatible surface), prompt/output parity (prompt-diff suite), latency & cost (p50/p95/p99 and $/1k tokens), and tokenization/edge-case behavior.
- Non-negotiables: audit logs and data controls, and an obvious fallback path to current endpoints during rollout.

Proposed two-week PoC (high level):
1) Day 0–2: Access & sample ingestion — you provide ~2k representative calls + 200 labeled examples (intent/expected output).
2) Day 3–5: OpenAI-compat smoke tests — run our compatibility shim against your sample set; flag any API surface mismatches (params, streaming behavior, function-calling).
3) Day 6–10: Quality diffs & prompt-diff suite — run prompt variants and generate regressions report; curate top 20 differences for manual review.
4) Day 11–14: Perf & cost matrix — p50/p95/p99, throughput limits, and estimated $/1M tokens on your workload; run a small SDK swap on a non-critical service to validate integration patterns.

Immediate asks from MayaTech:
- S3 link (or equivalent) with a sample of inference payloads and 200 labeled examples.
- A low-priv service account or temp credentials for sandbox access (we’ll treat everything as ephemeral).
- Point person for infra coordination (for networking/VPC if needed).

Ben and Karthik will lead the smoke tests and SDK-swap PoC respectively; Evelyn will own the quality/regression audit and dashboards. I’ve attached the call notes and a draft checklist for the PoC.

Can you confirm the dataset link and whether next Tuesday (Apr 19) for the first live sandbox run works for you?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

On Mon, Apr 12, 2027 at 3:02 PM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Can you confirm the dataset link and whether next Tuesday (Apr 19) for the first live sandbox run works for you?

Quick internal sync and a few clarifications / action items from my side:

Summary of what we should measure (concrete):
- API compatibility: request/response shape, param names (temperature, top_p, stop, logit_bias), streaming framing, function-calling payloads.
- Output parity: BLEU/ROUGE is noisy; we should use a task-specific metric + manual review for top N regressions (N=20).
- Performance: p50/p95/p99 latency matrix across payload length buckets (<=64, 65–512, >512 tokens).
- Cost: extrapolate tokenized request/response to $/1M tokens for Redwood Dedicated vs current hyperscaler run.

Owners & immediate next steps:
- Ben: run API-compat smoke tests and collect mismatches (Day 3–5).
- Karthik: prototype SDK swap on a small service; confirm necessary client-side edits (Day 6–10).
- Evelyn: set up quality dashboard + prompt-diff tooling, define review cadence (Day 6–12).
- Jordan: customer comms and escalation point.

Artifacts I’ll produce before we hit the sandbox:
- compatibility-checklist.xlsx (params & expected behaviors) — attached.
- latency-benchmark template and a simple pricing estimator.

One operational note: if MayaTech’s dataset includes long-context prompts (>2k tokens), we’ll need to include tests for KV-cache memory and quantify both latency and cost impacts.

I’ll drop the checklist and link the benchmark template to the shared Drive.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Jordan —

Thanks for the structured plan. We’re aligned on the goals. Provided below are the items you asked for and a few constraints from our side:

1) Dataset & access:
- S3 sample: s3://mayatech-eval/samples/mayatech-inference-sample-2027-04.zip
- Labeled examples folder inside the zip: /labeled/200-labeled.jsonl
- Temp creds: will share a short-lived IAM user (sending offline to your security contact).

2) Infra contact:
- Luca Bianchi (cc’d) will help with network/VPC access and firewall rules for the sandbox.

3) Constraints & notes:
- We cannot share PII-laden logs; the sample is redacted.
- We expect any integration work to avoid rewriting our client libraries if possible — prefer an OpenAI-compatible shim.

We’re good to start the sandbox on Tue Apr 19 at 10:00am PT. Please send an invite and any pre-req checklist for the run.

—Priya
